t:
(a) 
The first sentence of section 4(b) of the Urban Mass Transportation Act of 1964 is amended by striking out “$150, 000, 000 for fiscal year 1967” and inserting in lieu thereof “$150, 000, 000 for each of the fiscal years 1967, 1968, and 1969”.
 
    (b) 
Section 6(b) of such Act (redesignated section 6(c) by section 3 of this Act) is amended by striking out “and to $30, 000, 000 on July 1, 1966” and inserting in lieu thereof “to $30, 000, 000 on July 1, 1966, to $40, 000, 000 on July 1, 1967, and to $50, 000, 000 on July 1, 1968”.

fable.w: This section only amends dollar amounts and fiscal years in the appropriations authorizations of the Urban Mass Transportation Act of 1964. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Urban Mass Transportation Act to change the authorized appropriation amounts for specific fiscal years. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or the creation of an advisory body. It is a purely financial/administrative amendment.

qwen_block.b:
Temptation: The text mentions "Urban Mass Transportation Act" and amendments to it, which might imply some procedural change involving public input. However, the text itself only changes dollar amounts for appropriations.
Resolution: This section is purely an appropriation amendment, changing the amount of money authorized for specific fiscal years. It does not involve any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body with outside members. It is a straightforward budgetary adjustment.

opus.w: This section only changes funding amounts in the Urban Mass Transportation Act. No outside party is consulted, heard or given a right to object before a federal decision. Because the Act involves grants to localities, it might seem to involve outsiders, but grant funding and applications are not participation. Nothing in this text creates any process for outside involvement.
